subject: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 8:41 AM PT
Subject: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact

Sean —

For the Reliability Program weekly leadership readout, I want to make sure we’re aligned on:
1) the exact metrics we’ll report (definitions + how measured)
2) weekly cadence + where the “source of truth” lives
3) how we attribute impact from the incident bot + diagnostics project without over-claiming

My proposal is a single weekly snapshot with three sections:

A) Outcomes (incident-level)
- MTTR (P50/P90) for Sev0/Sev1, and separately for “customer-impacting” incidents
- Incident count by severity + region
- Time-to-suspect-change (median) for incidents where change correlation is applicable

B) Toil (on-call)
- Pager/alert volume (Sev0/1 pages + total pages)
- “Minutes of manual context gathering” proxy (see below) + responder sentiment note (1–2 bullets)

C) Initiative health (incident bot + diagnostics)
- Adoption: % Sev0/1 incidents where bot posted a context bundle within 2 minutes of incident start
- Bot reliability: bundle generation latency (P50/P95), collector error rate, partial bundle rate
- Quality: % of incidents with ≥1 “useful” feedback reaction, plus a short qualitative example

Questions / asks:
- Are you comfortable making “time-to-suspect-change” a top-line KPI? I think it’s a good leading indicator, but we need to be precise about how we compute it.
- For toil: do you prefer we use a lightweight responder tag (e.g., /bot-feedback + /toil-minutes) or keep it fully observational (Slack reactions + time spent in tools)?

I drafted a lightweight template for the weekly email + a standing doc where we keep definitions. Links:
- Reliability_Program_Weekly_Metrics_Template_v0.2 (Google Doc link)
- MTTR_baseline_and_toil_measurement_sheet (Drive link)

If you can reply with proposed definitions for:
- “Incident start time” (page time vs #incidents timestamp)
- “Suspect change time” (first message citing a deploy/config delta? first bot highlight?)
- “Bot posted within 2 minutes” (from incident creation to first bundle message)

…I’ll lock the format and we’ll start next Monday.

Thanks,
Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Exec Sponsor, Reliability Program
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Re: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact

Agree on the structure. A few notes/edits so we don’t get into definition wars mid-quarter:

1) Incident start time
- For Sev0/1: use PagerDuty incident “created_at” as canonical start.
- If PD is missing (rare), fall back to #incidents thread creation timestamp.

2) MTTR
- End time = “resolved_at” in PD.
- We should report separate MTTR for:
  (a) infrastructure/serving incidents
  (b) customer-specific incidents (ticket-driven), because the latter get dragged by customer comms.

3) Time-to-suspect-change
I’m okay with it as a KPI if we constrain when it applies:
- Only for incidents where there was a deploy/config change in the prior X window (e.g., 2h) AND where responders explicitly tagged it as the suspected trigger.
- We should NOT compute this from “first mention of deploy” in Slack. Too noisy.

I’d recommend:
- We add a lightweight responder tag in the #incidents thread: “suspect_change_at=<timestamp>” and “suspect_change_type=deploy|config|unknown”.
- The incident bot can prompt for it once per incident (e.g., after posting context bundle), but not spam.

4) Bot posted within 2 minutes
Define as: (timestamp of PD created_at) → (timestamp of first bot context bundle message in incident thread).
- For restricted incidents where full bundle posts elsewhere, count the restricted post time.

Toil measurement
I’d prefer an explicit quick tag rather than trying to infer time from tool usage:
- “/toil +N” command in the incident thread at resolve time (N = minutes spent on manual context gathering)
- Optional “/bot-useful yes/no” (or thumbs-up/down) to help segment impact.

Happy to review the weekly template; I can also have Rafael put together the first cut of the definitions doc in Confluence and link it.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Manager (Incident Workflow)
Redwood Inference



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact

This is good. Two follow-ups:

1) Time-to-suspect-change — I like the explicit responder tag. To avoid it becoming another “process tax”, can we make it:
- required only for Sev0 and Sev1
- one prompt from the bot near the end (“Before you close: tag suspected change + toil minutes”), and otherwise it’s voluntary

2) Weekly cadence / audience
I’m going to forward the weekly snapshot to exec staff + Eng leadership. It needs to be:
- consistent
- short (<= 10 bullets, plus 1 small table)
- no sensitive customer details

Can we align on:
- publish every Monday 10am PT (covering prior Mon–Sun)
- owner: SRE (Rafael) authors, Sean reviews, I forward
- include a link to a dashboard for those who want details, but keep the email digestible

If you’re okay, I’ll update the template with your definitions.

Neha



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 12:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact

All aligned.

On the “process tax” concern:
- We’ll limit required tagging to Sev0/Sev1.
- Bot prompt will be end-of-incident only, and it will be skippable.
- We’ll keep the schema dead simple:
  - /incident-metrics suspect_change=deploy|config|none|unknown
  - /incident-metrics suspect_change_at=now|<timestamp>
  - /incident-metrics toil_minutes=<int>
  - /incident-metrics bot_useful=yes|no

We can start with “/incident-metrics” as a slash command (or a message template the bot recognizes) and iterate.

Weekly cadence:
- Monday 10am PT works.
- Rafael can author; I’ll do a quick pass for consistency.
- For the table, I’d suggest:

  Sev0/1 incidents | MTTR P50 | MTTR P90 | Time-to-suspect-change (median) | Bot bundle <2m | Collector error rate

We’ll link:
- Linear ENG-2841 for initiative status
- the metrics definitions page in Confluence

I’ll ask Rafael to draft the definitions page today.

Sean



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 4:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil cadence + tracking incident bot impact

Perfect.

One more thing to bake into the weekly snapshot: a clear separation between:
- leading indicators (bundle posted <2m, bot/collector health, adoption)
- lagging outcomes (MTTR, pages, customer impact)

So when MTTR is flat for a week, we can still show we’re improving the inputs.

I updated the template doc accordingly and added a “notes / caveats” footer:
- time-to-suspect-change only computed for incidents with responder tagging
- restricted incidents: no details in the weekly email, only counted in aggregates

If Rafael posts the first definitions page, send me the link and I’ll use that as the canonical reference when forwarding updates.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Exec Sponsor, Reliability Program
Redwood Inference
